_meta.indication: Treatment of pediatric patients 1 year and older who weigh at least 11.5 kg and have growth failure due to inadequate secretion of endogenous growth hormone (GH).

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group study; subjects randomized 2:1 to lonapegsomatropin-tcgd or Genotropin (daily somatropin), dose 0.24 mg/kg/week in both arms.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naïve, prepubertal pediatric patients with growth hormone deficiency (GHD).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized Height Velocity (AHV) at Week 52, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 2 cm/year followed by a test of superiority.
pivotal_trials.result: By the sponsor's pre-specified ANCOVA analysis, AHV at Week 52 was 11.2 cm/year for SKYTROFA vs 10.3 cm/year for Genotropin; treatment difference 0.86 cm/year (95% CI 0.22, 1.50), p=0.009. The reviewer's single-imputation ANCOVA gave a treatment difference of 0.80 cm/year (95% CI 0.13, 1.47). Non-inferiority was met and statistical significance for superiority was achieved, but the treatment difference is small and the review cautions this study on its own may not provide sufficient evidence for a determination of superiority to another approved drug.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were viral infection (15% vs 11%), pyrexia (15% vs 9%), cough (11% vs 7%), nausea and vomiting (11% vs 7%), hemorrhage (7% vs 2%), diarrhea, abdominal pain, and arthralgia/arthritis. Serious class risks include intracranial hypertension, glucose intolerance/diabetes, hypoadrenalism, and slipped capital femoral epiphysis.
target_moa: A long-acting (pegylated) recombinant human growth hormone prodrug; somatropin binds the GH receptor to trigger signal transduction and IGF-1–mediated effects, stimulating skeletal growth at the growth plates of long bones.
modality: Other (pegylated recombinant human growth hormone / protein prodrug)

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions.

description.text: Added new indication for growth hormone replacement in adults with growth hormone deficiency

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for the addition of a new indication for the replacement of endogenous growth hormone in adults with growth hormone deficiency (GHD).

surrogate_endpoint.text: Approval was based on annualized growth velocity (AGV/AHV), a validated surrogate endpoint accepted at 1-2 year timepoints for GH products — this was a traditional (not accelerated) approval.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan-drug designation granted April 13, 2020 for the treatment of growth hormone deficiency.

citations.quote: On April 13, 2020, the Office of orphan products granted an orphan-drug designation to lonapegsomatropin-tcgd for the treatment of growth hormone deficiency.

basis.text: The applicant requested priority review, but the request was denied.

citations.quote: The submission also included a request for priority review based on the fact that pediatric GHD

is a serious condition and the Applicant's data demonstrated significant improvement in the effectiveness over Genotropin for treatment of pediatric GHD. This request was denied for following reasons: 1) the Applicant's clinical program completed to date did not evaluate the effect of the drug on a serious aspect of the condition; 2) there was no evidence to suggest that treatment with lonapegsomatropin-tc9d offers significant, clinically meaningful improvement in effectiveness (annualized growth velocity), or a better toxicity profile over the existing therapy; 3) there was no evidence that lonapegsomatropin-tc9d offers an improved compliance/adherence as a potential benefit over existing therapies, given the study was not designed to compare the adherence between two products, and to demonstrate that improved adherence improves annualized growth velocity as well as final adult height.

summary.text: Skytrofa was approved via traditional (non-accelerated) approval under Section 351(a) based on a single pivotal trial (CT-301) using annualized growth velocity, a validated surrogate endpoint. It received orphan-drug designation (April 13, 2020); a priority review request was denied; and it was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: On June 25, 2020 Ascendis Pharma submitted a Biologics License Application (BLA) for lonapegsomatropin-tcgd, a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) derivative, under Section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act in support of the following indication: Treatment of pediatric patients who have growth failure due growth hormone deficiency.
On April 13, 2020, the Office of orphan products granted an orphan-drug designation to lonapegsomatropin-tcgd for the treatment of growth hormone deficiency.

Your application for Skytrofa was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease.
